When using TEA I've had success getting yellow, green & blue holograms with also the added bonus of decreasing exposure time by half.

Is there anyway to keep the same reduced exposure time, but keeping the finished image at red??

posts.author: HoloM
posts.content_md: If you wash out the TEA and let the film dry before exposure, you should get a red image and a reduced exposure time. It may also be sufficient to wash the film in water and let it dry before exposure. I think preswelling with tea is not necessary.

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
[quote:6bb01a2903="HoloM"] I think preswelling with tea is not necessary.[/quote:6bb01a2903]

Presensitising is necessary, or certainly very desirable for BB plates but not for Slavich.

I've had some success with Ammonia as a presensitiser. This will presensitise without preswelling. The advantage is that you don't get the problems of streaks and blotches from a washed, pre-exposed plate.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
> **tpark:** What concentration/time do you use with ammonia? I'd like to try the bb-640 plates as masters, so I don't need preswelling for this, but I need presensitization.It's possible to get holograms without presensitization, but it takes a lot less energy to expose the plates once they've been TEA soaked. Is the exposure energy for ammonia presensitizing about the same as for TEA?

From a July post: "If the color shift is not wanted, or if you have no TEA (triethanolamine), you could try presoaking in 1% ammonia solution. (Dinesh's suggestion) I just diluted household ammonia (not BLEACH!) with distilled water. Use an airtight container - the stuff is very stinky. I found it gave sensitivity [roughly] equivalent to TEA with no color shift, but with slight fogging (darkening of unexposed areas). As a TEA alternative, you could experiment with ammonia + something else (corn syrup or sugar?) to preswell the emulsion."

I soaked for 2-3 minutes. The household ammonia concentration was not known, so I assumed it was 30% and diluted 30:1. I now know it is more likely to be in the range of 5 to 10% ([http://www.csupomona.edu/~jskoga/Aquariums/Ammonia.html](http://www.csupomona.edu/~jskoga/Aquariums/Ammonia.html))

so I was really only using a 0.15% to 0.3% ammonia soak. Probably even less will work OK, which might reduce fogging. Also washing before development might help with this, though as noted, fogging is not very severe anyway.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
I have washed out the TEA many times. It works just fine. I give the plate a 2 minute soak in distilled water and I have had no problems with replay color shift.

Blue is another story. I have not been able to make consistantly bright blue holograms with a HeNe. Does anyone have some advice? I have tried different TEA concentrations times all with PFG-01.

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md: I've done it with Agfa 8E75, but never with Slavich or BB. With Agfa, I soaked in about 6% TEA for about 5 minutes, then squeegeed. Unfortunately going from red to blue really strains the emulsion almost to breaking point. Another problem may be with grain density, as opposed to grain size. If the grain density is low then expanding the emulsion depth may take the grains too far apart to take the higher spatial frequencies. As a rough calculation shows, blue needs a fringe seperation of 200 odd nm, which translates to 5000 l/mm.
